bibliography.abstract: Travel planning agents assist users in generating personalized travel plans by modeling their individual preferences. Existing agents either rely on explicit user instructions or engage in multi-turn clarification to elicit user preferences. However, both approaches overlook the rich behavioral signals latent in users' past behaviors, which implicitly encode their preferences. This over-reliance on active user input increases interaction burden and limits plan personalization. To bridge this gap, we introduce a new task, Behavior-Aware Travel Planning, which infers user preferences directly from past behaviors and generates personalized travel plans. To facilitate research on this task, we introduce Behavior2Trip, a benchmark constructed from one of the largest Chinese online travel platforms, comprising 11,400 instances. Each instance represents an average of 39.8 past user behaviors spanning 14 attributes across 5 preference dimensions. We further propose B2T-Agent, a reinforcement learning-based agent that leverages user behavior trajectories, interacts with external tools for preference-aligned retrieval, and maintains an internal memory module. Experiments on Behavior2Trip show that GPT-4.1 achieves a full-constraint pass rate of only 0.5\% on the hardest tasks, while B2T-Agent built upon Qwen3-8B outperforms all baselines, highlighting the substantial challenge of this task. Moreover, Qwen3-8B trained with B2T-Agent also outperforms GPT-4.1 on the TravelPlanner benchmark, demonstrating strong generalization. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUAA-IRIP-LLM/Behavior2Trip
bibliography.title: Behavior2Trip: Towards Personalized Travel Planning via User Behavior Trajectory

en.caveats: The benchmark data is sourced from a single Chinese online travel platform, which may reflect specific regional travel habits and platform-specific user behaviors.
en.what: The researchers established a new task, Behavior-Aware Travel Planning, and built the Behavior2Trip benchmark using 11,400 instances from a major Chinese online travel platform, where each instance averages 39.8 past user behaviors across 14 attributes. They developed B2T-Agent, a reinforcement learning-based agent that uses behavior trajectories, external retrieval tools, and an internal memory module. While GPT-4.1 achieved a full-constraint pass rate of only 0.5% on the hardest tasks within the benchmark, the Qwen3-8B model trained with B2T-Agent outperformed all baselines and demonstrated strong generalization on the external TravelPlanner benchmark.
en.why: It shifts personalized travel planning away from relying on active, burdensome user inputs or multi-turn clarifications, proving instead that rich, latent preferences can be extracted directly from historical behavior trajectories.
